battle.name: 第一次麥西尼亞戰爭
battle.brief: 公元前八世紀中葉，斯巴達王阿爾卡美涅斯奪下米塞尼亞邊境重鎮安斐亞，二十年戰爭隨即爆發。米塞尼亞人推舉阿里斯托德莫斯為統帥，退守伊托墨山，靠大壕溝與短柄投槍手屢挫斯巴達前鋒。斯巴達終於攻陷伊托墨，土地被按份分封，米塞尼亞人自此淪為黑字者。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 第一次米塞尼亞戰爭是公元前八世紀中葉斯巴達與米塞尼亞之間的一場全面戰爭，交戰地帶在伯羅奔尼撒島南部，以塔伊格特斯山脊為天然分界，核心是米塞尼亞的安斐亞、伊托墨山與山北的米塞尼亞平原。斯巴達一方是拉科尼亞的城邦聯盟，主力為斯巴達公民兵：重裝步兵肩並肩成排，隊長居中，兩翼由庇里阿斯城邦提供的輕裝步兵與射手補足；國王與長老院決定戰略方向。斯巴達採雙王制，提奧彭波斯與其弟波利多洛斯分掌兩條戰線，另有三十人長老院與五名監察官握有發動戰爭與徵召的實權；這套指揮系統在漫長戰事中的運作遲緩，本身就是戰爭被拖長的重要原因。米塞尼亞一方是全境自由民組成的聯盟軍，平時為農、戰時為兵，推舉一位集中全部權力的統帥阿里斯托德莫斯，其任期終身、處置不受節制，這在希臘城邦的制度史上前所未見。米塞尼亞沒有常備軍，也沒有騎兵，兵源明顯多於斯巴達的常備公民兵，卻缺乏重裝步兵所需的訓練與金屬裝備。兩軍對照之下，一方長於組織與裝備，一方長於人數、地形與消耗能力，這正是這場戰爭能夠延續二十年的根本原因。
countriesEn: The First Messenian War was a general war fought between Sparta and Messenia in the middle of the eighth century BC. The theatre lay in the south of the Peloponnese, with the ridge of Mount Taygetus as a natural divide, and centred on Ampheia, on Mount Ithome and on the plain of Messenia to the north of the mountain. On the Spartan side stood a league of the cities of Laconia, whose main strength was the Spartan citizen body: heavy infantry drawn up shoulder to shoulder, with file leaders in the centre and light infantry and archers supplied by the perioikic towns on the flanks, while the kings and the council of elders set the strategic direction. Sparta worked with a dual kingship, with Theopompus and his brother Polydorus holding the two lines of command, and with a council of thirty elders and five ephors holding the real power to declare war and to call up the levy. The sluggish working of that command system across a long campaign was itself an important reason the war dragged on. On the Messenian side stood an allied force of free men from the whole territory, farmers in peace and soldiers in war, who chose a single commander who was given undivided military and civil authority: Aristodemus, whose term was for life and whose decisions were unappealable. This was without precedent in the institutional history of the Greek city states. Messenia had no standing army and no cavalry, its numerical superiority over the Spartan citizen levy was clear, and it lacked the training and the metal equipment that heavy infantry demanded. Set side by side, the two sides were strong in opposite ways, one in organisation and equipment, the other in numbers, terrain and endurance, and that contrast is the root reason the war could last twenty years.
people: 這場戰爭留下的人名，主要來自二世紀潘薩尼亞斯《希臘風土志》第四卷，以及斯巴達與米塞尼亞的詩歌傳統，可信度並不相同，須分層看待。斯巴達方面，製造導火線的人最具決定性：國王阿爾卡美涅斯在一次襲擊中攻下米塞尼亞邊境重鎮安斐亞，佔領之後不作撤離，等於向全境宣戰；他後來陣亡或病逝，斯巴達人問策於德爾斐神諭，得到聽從女子勸告這類含混的指示。接替他的是提奧彭波斯與波利多洛斯兩位國王，前者在位約前七六〇–七二〇年，後者約前七四五–七二五年，戰爭通常繫於波利多洛斯在位的第一年，即前七四三年前後。傳說中的末代阿吉亞德王提薩美諾斯在戰中陣亡或退位，其子阿納克桑德繼位，戰事仍繼續下去。米塞尼亞方面的核心人物是阿里斯托德莫斯：米塞尼亞人推舉他為統帥，賦予不加分割的軍政大權，他率軍退守伊托墨山，主持大壕溝的挖掘與突圍；戰後他的下落眾說紛紜，有人說他帶殘部渡海遠走，有人說他留在山裡直到最後。接手的是克里俄提斯，傳記中他在戰局最壞時接任，曾試圖在拉科尼亞另闢戰線。文學上另有兩位重要人物：詩人提爾泰俄斯，據說斯巴達人因需要戰歌而向雅典求援，得到回應是派他前往；以及記錄整場戰爭的潘薩尼亞斯本人，他是二世紀的旅行者，所記述的很多場面帶有傳說色彩。群體角色同樣關鍵：庇里阿斯步兵與射手、拉科尼亞的援軍、替軍隊搬運糧食的隨從，以及米塞尼亞的農兵與投槍手。
peopleEn: The names attached to this war come mainly from the fourth book of the Description of Greece that Pausanias wrote in the second century AD, and from the poetic tradition of Sparta and Messenia. Their credibility differs, and they have to be read in layers. On the Spartan side the maker of the immediate occasion was the decisive figure: King Alcamenes took Ampheia, a border town of Messenia, on a raid and did not withdraw afterwards, which amounted to a declaration of war against the whole country. He was later killed or died, and the Spartans consulted the oracle at Delphi, receiving a vague instruction of the kind to heed the counsel of women. He was succeeded in command by the two kings Theopompus, who reigned about 760 to 720 BC, and Polydorus, about 745 to 725 BC, and the war is usually attached to the first year of Polydorus, that is to about 743 BC. In the tradition the last Agiad king, Tisamenus, was killed in the fighting or abdicated, and his son Anaxander succeeded him while the war went on. On the Messenian side the central figure is Aristodemus. The Messenians chose him as their commander and gave him undivided authority over army and state; he led the retreat to Mount Ithome, directed the digging of the Great Trench and the breakout. His fate after the war is variously reported, some saying he carried the survivors away overseas and others that he stayed on the hill to the end. He was followed by Cleonnis, who in the account took over when the situation was at its worst and tried to open a second front in Laconia. Two further figures matter on the literary side: the poet Tyrtaeus, whom the Spartans are said to have asked Athens for when they needed a war poem, and who was sent in response, and Pausanias himself, the second-century traveller whose narrative carries a strong legendary colouring. Group figures matter as much: the perioikic infantry and archers, the allied contingents, the porters who carried grain for the army, and the Messenian farmers and spear-throwers.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長矛是公元前九世紀兩河流域的形制：短柄、長刃、鐵鏃，亞述人把它與弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。把它放回公元前八世紀的伯羅奔尼撒，就必須老實說明：希臘世界此時的矛頭仍以青銅為主，鐵是稀罕金屬，價高而難鍛，數量極少，因此米塞尼亞與斯巴達的矛兵在功能上最接近卡面這件兵器的，是短柄投槍：木柄纏皮帶以便脫手，槍頭為青銅，擲出後可以回收再用，配小圓盾，戰士不必穿重甲。斯巴達重裝步兵的標準裝備是圓盾（希臘語稱重裝盾，後來「重裝步兵」一詞即由它而來）、青銅頭盔、青銅護脛、青銅胸甲、短劍與雙刃斧，加長矛與數支標槍；米塞尼亞步兵則以投槍、小盾、弓箭與石彈為主，鎧甲極少，頭盔多靠繳獲敵軍。攻城與防禦器械方面，據記載斯巴達人用過一輛載滿士兵的伊達戰車去填塞米塞尼亞人挖的大壕溝，車上所載人數相傳約三百，壕溝因此被填平；米塞尼亞人則以削尖木樁、落石、陷坑與縱火作防禦，並派熟悉山徑的小隊繞到敵後斷糧。交通與後勤方面，兩軍都靠步行、驢馬與牛車，糧食由米塞尼亞的田地與對拉科尼亞的掠奪供給；斯巴達那條短距離的運補線，在圍城階段反而成為米塞尼亞最有效的作用目標。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card is a form from the ninth century BC Mesopotamia: a short shaft, a long blade and an iron head, and the Assyrians bound it together with the bow and with iron work as one city after another fell in the two riverlands. Set back in the Peloponnese of the eighth century BC, it has to be said honestly that the spearheads of the Greek world were still overwhelmingly bronze, that iron was a rare and expensive metal, hard to forge and produced in small quantity. The closest functional equivalent of the weapon on the card in Messenia and Sparta was therefore the short throwing spear, the sauroter: a wooden shaft wound with a leather thong so that it could be released, a bronze head, a weapon that could be recovered and reused, and one carried with a small round shield by men who did not wear heavy armour. The standard kit of the Spartan heavy infantry was the round shield, the aspis, from which the word hoplite is derived, together with a bronze helmet, bronze greaves, a bronze corselet, a short sword and a double axe, together with the long spear and a few javelins. The Messenian foot carried throwing spears, small shields, bows and stones, with very little body armour and with helmets largely taken from captured enemy kit. For siege and defence the Spartans are said to have used a war chariot loaded with soldiers to fill the Great Trench the Messenians had dug, the car carrying by tradition some three hundred men, so that the trench could be levelled. The Messenians answered with sharpened stakes, rock slides, pits and fire, and sent small bands who knew the mountain paths around to the enemy's rear to cut his supplies. In movement and supply both armies depended on foot, mules and ox carts, and the grain came from the fields of Messenia and from what could be taken in Laconia, which in the siege phase made the short supply line of Sparta the most effective target for the Messenians.
tactics: 斯巴達的戰術是典型的希臘城邦重裝步兵作戰：列陣、接戰、正面猛推。兩軍以圓盾互相抵住，矛兵從盾後伸矛刺擊，靠齊整的陣形與體力對拼分出勝負，往往幾個時辰內見分明；斯巴達不習慣追擊潰敵，也不在敵前久滯，一旦無法正面取勝，就轉向圍城、斷糧與拆散對手的盟邦，這是斯巴達最擅長的辦法。米塞尼亞的戰術完全相反：避免正面會戰，退入山區，盡量延長戰爭。戰事初期，米塞尼亞人屢次進入拉科尼亞境內，摧毀田園與正在成熟的作物，迫使斯巴達分散兵力和守備點，使對方的絕對優勢無法一次發揮。戰爭第五年，米塞尼亞人在伊托墨山挖出足以陷住重裝步兵的大壕溝，以枝葉覆蓋偽裝，斯巴達人用伊達戰車把壕溝填平，第六年米塞尼亞人趁隙突圍，轉戰拉科尼亞，再退入伊托墨山堡，據守約三年，靠掠奪拉科尼亞維持，最後因糧食耗盡與疫病而屈服。指揮與控制方面，斯巴達有牛角號與嚴格的戰前訓令，但雙王分立、程序繁複；米塞尼亞有一位權力不受節制的統帥，調動與決斷反而快得多。季節方面，戰爭橫跨多個收成週期，希臘各城邦的征戰多在夏秋展開；本目錄所填月份為推定，文獻並無記載。
tacticsEn: The Spartan method was the standard Greek city state heavy infantry action: deploy, make contact, push hard on the front. The two armies locked shields, the spearmen thrust from behind the shield wall, and the result was settled by the regularity of the formation and by physical endurance, usually within a few hours. Sparta was not in the habit of pursuing a broken enemy or of lingering in the open before the enemy; when it could not win head-on it turned to siege, to cutting supply and to breaking up the allies of its opponent, which was what Sparta did best. The Messenian tactics were the exact opposite: avoid a general engagement, fall back into the hills and make the war as long as possible. In the early years the Messenians repeatedly entered Laconia, destroying fields and ripening crops, which forced the Spartans to disperse their troops and their garrisons and denied them the chance to concentrate their superiority in a single stroke. In the fifth year of the war the Messenians dug on Mount Ithome a trench deep and wide enough to trap heavy infantry, and disguised it with brushwood; the Spartans levelled it with the Idaean chariot, and in the sixth year the Messenians broke out through the gap, raided Laconia and withdrew again into the fortress on Ithome, where they held out for about three years on what they could take from Laconia, and finally yielded when food ran out and disease spread. As for command, Sparta had its horn signals and its strict pre-battle orders, but the two kings were divided and the procedure formal; Messenia had a commander whose power was unchecked, which made movement and decision far faster. As for the season, the war ran through several harvest cycles, and Greek campaigns generally fell in summer and autumn; the month entered in this record is inferred, since no source records it.
data: 可核對的數字分幾類，而且都要打折看待。年表方面：戰爭列表把此役繫於公元前七四〇年，主流學界一般寫作約前七四三–七二四年；潘薩尼亞斯說戰爭歷時二十年，並以斯巴達王波利多洛斯在位第一年為起點，波利多洛斯的在位年分約前七四五–七二五年，提奧彭波斯約前七六〇–七二〇年，末代阿吉亞德王提薩美諾斯的年代則眾說紛紜。戰役節奏有明確的年序：第五年挖掘大壕溝，第六年突圍，之後在伊托墨山據守約三年，第十九與二十年之間以圍攻與飢餓迫降。器械方面有兩個可引的數目：填壕的伊達戰車所載人數相傳約三百；以及斯巴達方面相傳把米塞尼亞人阿里斯托德莫斯的盾牌與伊達的木盆奉獻於奧林匹克的祭典，人物與器物都帶傳說色彩。土地與人口方面，斯巴達在戰後將米塞尼亞土地按份分配，斯巴達人自留其中一部分（相傳約五分之一），其餘分給公民；米塞尼亞人留在原地成為黑字者，並未被整批遷走。兵力數字則完全不可考：兩軍人數從未被可靠文獻記載，斯巴達一方常被形容為人少而精，米塞尼亞一方靠人口與民兵補充，任何具體的傷亡與俘虜數字都應視為文學加工，不可引用。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into several classes, and all of them have to be discounted. Chronology first: the list of battles ties this war to 740 BC, while mainstream scholarship usually writes it as about 743 to 724 BC. Pausanias says the war lasted twenty years and takes its beginning from the first year of the Spartan king Polydorus, whose reign is dated about 745 to 725 BC, while Theopompus is placed at about 760 to 720 BC; the date of the last Agiad king, Tisamenus, is variously given. The sequence of the campaign is clearly marked: the Great Trench was dug in the fifth year, the breakout came in the sixth, the holdout on Ithome lasted about three years, and surrender was forced by siege and hunger in the nineteenth and twentieth years. Two figures can be cited from the equipment: the Idaean chariot that filled the trench carried by tradition some three hundred men, and the Spartans are said to have dedicated the shield of the Messenian Aristodemus together with the wooden bowl of Ida at the games of Olympia, though both the person and the objects carry a legendary colouring. As for land and population, after the war Sparta divided the Messenian land into lots, keeping a portion itself, said to be about a fifth, and distributing the rest to citizens; the Messenians stayed where they were and became helots rather than being moved off the land. Numbers of men cannot be checked at all: no reliable document records the sizes of either army, the Spartan side is commonly described as few but well equipped, the Messenian side drew on population and militia, and any specific figures for casualties and prisoners should be treated as literary fabrication and not quoted.
cause: 打起來的直接原因在史料裡寫得很清楚：斯巴達王阿爾卡美涅斯率隊攻下米塞尼亞的邊境城鎮安斐亞，佔領之後不作撤離，等於向米塞尼亞全境宣戰，戰爭從此開始。但一次襲擊只是導火線，底下還有更長的結構。第一是土地：塔伊格特斯山脊兩側的米塞尼亞平原是伯羅奔尼撒島最肥沃的耕地與牧場，邊界在古人的地圖上相當模糊，兩邊農民長期互相越界，牧群與田界爭執不斷。第二是生存結構：斯巴達的土地有限、公民兵人數有限，擴張的方式只有奪取外部土地；而米塞尼亞人一方面受斯巴達人侵擾，另一方面也習慣性地掠奪拉科尼亞的田產，這使衝突具備週期性。第三是神話與儀式：相傳斯巴達人曾求問神諭，得到直到正午投下影子這類邊界答覆，並有在阿米克萊與阿爾基亞定期出擊米塞尼亞的儀式；對斯巴達而言，戰爭不只是軍事行動，也是祭儀。第四是米塞尼亞的社會：米塞尼亞是全境自由民社會，沒有斯巴達那種依附城邦的黑字者階層，國民兵動員快、團結程度高，這使它在正面不敵時仍能以持久戰應對。學界對這場戰爭是否真如晚出史料所述延續二十年仍有保留，但前八世紀的斯巴達與米塞尼亞之間發生過反覆衝突這件事本身，幾乎沒有爭議。
causeEn: The immediate cause is set down plainly in the sources. King Alcamenes of Sparta took the Messenian border town of Ampheia in a raid and did not withdraw, which was a declaration of war against the whole of Messenia, and the war began there. But a raid is only the trigger; beneath it lie longer structures. The first is land. The Messenian plain on the Taygetus side was the most fertile arable and pasture land in the Peloponnese, the boundary was vague on ancient maps, the farmers of the two sides habitually crossed it, and quarrels over grazing and residual field boundaries never stopped. The second is the structure of subsistence: land in Sparta was limited and the number of citizens was limited, so the only way to expand was to take land from outside, while on the other side Messenians were themselves in the habit of raiding the fields of Laconia, which made the conflict cyclical. The third is myth and ritual: the Spartans are said to have consulted an oracle and received a boundary answer of the kind until a man casts his shadow at noon, and there was a periodic ritual of striking into Messenia at Amyclae and at Algea; for Sparta war was not only a military operation but a rite. The fourth is Messenian society. Messenia was a society of free men over its whole territory, without the class of helots attached to the city that Sparta had, so its citizens could be mobilised quickly and held together well, which is what allowed it to answer a superior enemy with a war of attrition. Scholars still debate whether the war really lasted the twenty years the late sources describe, but that there were repeated conflicts between Sparta and Messenia in the eighth century BC is very nearly uncontested.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果，最深的一層是改變了斯巴達的社會結構。米塞尼亞人戰敗後沒有被滅族，而是留在自己的土地上成為黑字者，綁在土地上的佃戶；這項安排讓斯巴達的農業產出可以支撐一支不事生產的公民戰士階層，於是斯巴達得以長期以少數人口維持壓倒性的軍事力量。第二層是它提供了希臘世界最早的消耗戰範本：以游擊破壞經濟、以退守山區拖長戰線、以拒絕正面會戰對抗裝備與訓練的差距，後來第二次米塞尼亞戰爭幾乎照搬這套做法，斯巴達也據此發展出更完整的圍城與守備手段。第三層是對斯巴達內部的刺激：戰爭暴露了公民兵人數不足與土地分配不均的問題，傳說中的提奧彭波斯改革與所謂未能完成的改革，背景都指向米塞尼亞戰爭之後的焦慮；後來斯巴達內部關於土地分配與黑字者體制的爭議，從克雷奧梅涅斯一世時期的土地集中措施，到前四六四年前後那場規模浩大的黑字者密謀，也常被拉回這段歷史裡比較。第四層是記憶與文本：米塞尼亞人的戰敗被寫進奧林匹克的儀式傳說，包括阿里斯托德莫斯的盾牌、對祭牲內臟分食權的主張，以及一位失去兒子的米塞尼亞母親的故事；潘薩尼亞斯的《風土志》第四卷因而成為這場戰爭的主要載體，亞里士多德在《政治學》第五卷裡把它當作民眾授權絕對權力救國的先例來引用，於是這場前古典的戰爭，反而在政治思想史上留下了比在戰爭史上更長的迴響。
impactEn: The deepest consequence of the war was a change in the social structure of Sparta. The defeated Messenians were not exterminated but left on their own land as helots, tenants bound to the soil, and that arrangement allowed the agricultural output of Messenia to support a citizen warrior class that did no production, so that Sparta was able to sustain overwhelming military force from a small population over the long run. The second layer is that the war supplied the earliest Greek model of war of attrition: harassment of the economy, withdrawal into the mountains to stretch the line of operations, and a refusal to accept battle in order to offset a gap in equipment and training. The Second Messenian War very nearly copied this method, and Sparta answered it with a more complete repertoire of siege and garrison. The third layer is the stimulus it gave to debate inside Sparta. The war exposed the shortage of citizen soldiers and the unevenness of land distribution; the reform attributed to Theopompus, and the so-called unfinished reform, both point back to the anxiety that followed the Messenian wars; and the later arguments inside Sparta over land distribution and the helot system, from the land-concentrating measures of Cleomenes I to the great helot conspiracy dated to around 464 BC, are also commonly drawn back to this stretch of history. The fourth layer is memory and text. The defeat of the Messenians was written into the ritual tradition of the games: the shield of Aristodemus, the claim to the distribution of the sacrificial splanchna, and the story of a Messenian mother who had lost her son. The fourth book of Pausanias became the main vehicle for the war because of it, and Aristotle in the fifth book of the Politics cites the case as a precedent of a people entrusting unlimited power to one man to save the state, so that this pre-classical war left a longer echo in the history of political thought than in the history of warfare.
result: 第二十年，米塞尼亞屈服。伊托墨山堡被攻下，聯盟軍解散，領袖的下落沒有一致的說法：有的記載說阿里斯托德莫斯帶著殘部渡海遠走，有的說他留在山裡直到最後；戰後斯巴達人相傳把米塞尼亞的盾牌連同伊達的木盆奉獻於奧林匹克的宙斯祭，說法本身也帶著神話色彩。對斯巴達而言，結果是明確的戰術與戰略勝利：以有限的人口拖住米塞尼亞的全民抵抗，最終在消耗戰中取勝；對米塞尼亞而言則是徹底的失敗，土地被按份分配給斯巴達公民，斯巴達人自留一部分，其餘分封，而米塞尼亞人留在原地成為黑字者，始終沒有得到斯巴達當初許諾過的平分份地位。這份落差成為米塞尼亞人世代累積的不滿，最終在六十餘年後引爆第二次米塞尼亞戰爭。就戰爭史本身而言，這一場留下幾個明確的示範：以少對多的持久戰是可行的，但代價漫長；退守山區加陷坑，是對付重裝矛陣的有效手段；斯巴達式的圍城與斷糧，最終壓過了游擊與掠奪所能買到的拖延。而整場戰爭最大的教訓，落在那件兵器上：長矛無論是亞述人配鐵鏃的短柄長刃，還是希臘人配青銅頭的投槍，本質上都靠人把它舉穩、把它擲準、把它插進對方的身體，而決定勝負的從來不是矛，而是站在矛後面的人，以及他們願意撐多久。
resultEn: In the twentieth year Messenia yielded. The fortress on Mount Ithome was taken, the allied army dissolved, and the fate of its leader is not reported consistently: some accounts have Aristodemus carrying the survivors away overseas, others have him staying on the hill to the last, and the Spartans are said to have dedicated the Messenian shield together with the wooden bowl of Ida to Zeus at Olympia, a claim that is itself mythic in colouring. For Sparta the result was an unambiguous tactical and strategic success. A small population had worn down a general resistance by Messenia and won in the end through a war of exhaustion. For Messenia it was a complete defeat: the land was divided into lots and given to Spartan citizens, the Spartans keeping a portion for themselves and distributing the rest, while the Messenians stayed and became helots, never receiving the equal share that Sparta had originally promised them. That gap became a grievance accumulated by the Messenians over generations and finally broke out in the Second Messenian War a little over sixty years later. For the history of warfare this war left several clear demonstrations: a protracted war against a stronger opponent is possible, but it is expensive; withdrawal into the hills combined with pits and traps is an effective answer to a heavy spear line; and the Spartan methods of siege and of cutting supply eventually outweighed the delay bought by harassment and plunder. And the largest lesson of the whole war lies on the weapon itself. Whether a short shaft with an iron blade in the hands of the Assyrians or a bronze-headed throwing spear in the hands of the Greeks, a spear is in the end only as good as the hand that holds it steady, that throws it true and drives it into the body of the enemy, and what decided the issue was never the spear but the men standing behind it, and how long they were willing to hold.
